S.I, Special Branch. 22 3 37
REPORT
Date March 22, 1937.

Subject "Shanghai Novosti", new Russian daily.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by I. Boyne. D.S.I.

A new Russian daily newspaper entitled "Shanghai Novosti"
(Shanghai Daily News) made its first appearance on March 20,
1937. It is published by M. Ya. Sibriakoff & Co., and edited
by Mr. N.A. Schegoleff. The editorial and printing offices
are situated at 612 Avenue Foch (Settlement side). Among
members of the staff there are several former collaborators of
the "Novy Put", local Russian daily, which ceased to appear
about two weeks ago owing to financial difficulties.

The following extracts from editorial articles which
appeared in the first issue of the newspaper in question contain
statements regarding its intended policy:-

"With regard to information which will be published in our
newspaper it must be pointed out that we have decided to abandon
the usual trend of emigrants' newspapers and to bring our news-
paper nearer to the American standard. It will not contain un-
necessary discussions of high politics, but will furnish real
information, real news from which an attentive reader will draw
his own conclusions."

"We will not attempt to teach our readers, to force our own
ideas upon them. The "Shanghai Daily News" will in the first
place endeavour to satisfy the sound curiosity of readers and
to help them to spend their leisure hours in a pleasant and
useful manner."

"Besides, taking into consideration the hard economic
conditions of our fellow-countrymen abroad, we will render every
assistance to them not by word, but by deed."

"We endeavour to create a newspaper of non-political cha-
racter, well informed and furnishing excellent information.
Our principal aim is to bring about the unification of Russian

报告
日期：1937年3月22日。

主题：“Shanghai Novosti”（《上海新闻》），新办俄文日报。

制作人：特别股督察普罗科菲耶夫 (D.S.I. Prokofiev) 转呈人：特别股督察博伊恩 (I. Boyne)。

一份名为“Shanghai Novosti”（《上海新闻》）的新办俄文日报于1937年3月20日首次发行。该报由 M. Ya. Sibriakoff & Co. 出版，N.A. Schegoleff 先生担任编辑。编辑部及印刷所位于福煦路612号（租界一侧）。在工作人员中，有几位是前俄文日报《Novy Put》（《新路》）的前合作者，该报因财务困难于约两周前停刊。

以下摘录自该报首期社论文章，其中包含关于其既定方针的声明：

“关于本报将刊登的信息，必须指出，我们已决定摒弃流亡报刊的惯常倾向，使我们的报纸更接近美国标准。本报不会包含对高层政治的不必要讨论，而是提供真实的信息、真实的新闻，细心的读者可从中得出自己的结论。”

“我们将不试图教导读者，也不强加我们的观点给他们。《上海新闻》将首先致力于满足读者健康的求知欲，并帮助他们以愉快且有益的方式度过闲暇时光。”

“此外，考虑到我们海外同胞严峻的经济状况，我们将通过实际行动而非空言向他们提供一切援助。”

“我们努力创办一份非政治性质、消息灵通并提供优质信息的报纸。我们的主要目标是促成俄罗斯

（左侧手写批注：*26457）
（左侧印章：特别股 / 1937年3月22日 / 上海公共租界工部局警务处）

"Thus, our slogan is : - information, real assistance to
Russian residents in Shanghai and eliminating dissensions
among them."
M. Ya. Sibiriskoff, Russian, arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin in 1931. He is a lithographer by profession and is
reported to have been working in this capacity in Harbin for
over 16 years. In Shanghai he was employed as manager of the
Union Press, 54/56 Nanking Road in 1933 - 1934. Sibiriskoff
is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118
Moulmein Road. While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice
of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an
undesirable character.
M.P. Netchkin, who forms the subject of file D-709 in
connection with his pro-Soviet attitude, is a partner of
Sibiriskoff & Company.
The "Shanghai Daily News" will be taken by this section.

“因此，我们的口号是：——提供信息，向在上海的俄罗斯居民提供实际援助，并消除他们之间的分歧。”
M. Ya. Sibiriskoff，俄国人，于1931年从哈尔滨抵达上海。他的职业是石版印刷工，据称在哈尔滨从事此职超过16年。在上海，他于1933年至1934年间受雇为南京路54/56号联合印刷厂 (Union Press) 的经理。Sibiriskoff 已在莫尔缅路118号俄罗斯侨民委员会登记。他在上海期间，未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。
M.P. Netchkin 是 Sibiriskoff & Company 的合伙人，因其亲苏态度而成为档案 D-709 的调查对象。

Shanghai Daily News,
612 Avenue Foch,
Tel. No. 36208,
Shanghai.

(Undated).

The Secretary,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that as from
to-day we have commenced the publication of a daily
Russian paper called "Shanghai Daily News" under the
editorship of Mr. N.A. Shchogolev, Messrs. M.J. Sibiriakov
& Co. - publishers.

The address of the editorial and publishing
office is at No.612, Avenue Foch, Tel. No.36208.

I am forwarding for your information the first
copy of the paper just published.

I trust that you will favour us with any information
that may be of interest to the general public and to your
Council.

I have the honour to be, Sir,
Yours faithfully,
(Sgd) N. Shchogolev
Editor.
